original_question: On which chromosome is the gene responsible for Cockayne syndrome type B located?

final_qi.question: On which chromosome is the gene responsible for Cockayne syndrome type B located?
final_qi.long_answer: Cockayne syndrome type B is caused by mutations in the ERCC6 (CSB) gene, which maps to the long arm of chromosome 10 (10q11.23). This gene encodes a DNA repair protein essential for transcription-coupled nucleotide-excision repair, and its disruption leads to the clinical features of Cockayne syndrome type B.
